name: European praying mantis
title: A leg that folds like a pocketknife
overview: Open a grasping leg slowly. Watch the two rows of spines separate as the shin swings away from the thigh.
dragHint: Drag a front leg up to open it
gestureGuide: Drag either front leg up or outward to open it, then reverse your drag to fold it. Each leg holds its own position.

parts.name: Head capsule
parts.short: Look at the triangle between the two big eyes.
parts.detail: The broad upper head narrows toward the chewing mouth. Pull away the capsule to find the brain behind the eyes.

parts.name: Long neck shield
parts.short: The long green shield behind the head is part of the chest.
parts.detail: It covers the first thoracic segment, which carries the grasping legs. The shield widens near their attachment.

parts.name: Wing-bearing chest
parts.short: The wings and four walking legs meet here.
parts.detail: The middle and rear thoracic segments carry the two pairs of wings. They are shown as one selectable unit.

parts.name: Simple eyes
parts.short: Find three tiny eyes between the two large ones.
parts.detail: These simple light sensors form a triangle on the face, distinct from the faceted compound eyes.

parts.name: Left compound eye
parts.short: Many tiny windows look out from one big eye.
parts.detail: Each facet admits light in a particular direction. The dark patch represents a pseudopupil in this fixed view.

parts.name: Left feeler
parts.short: A long thread on the head helps sense the surroundings.
parts.detail: The thick basal segments support a slender flagellum. Its many small articles are simplified here.

parts.name: Left chewing jaw
parts.short: Two jaws meet sideways to cut a bite.
parts.detail: The paired mandibles sit below the face. Their hardened edges work against each other.

parts.name: Left mouth feeler
parts.short: This little finger feels food near the mouth.
parts.detail: The segmented palp belongs to a maxilla. Its tip samples material beside the mandibles.

parts.name: Right compound eye
parts.short: Many tiny windows look out from one big eye.
parts.detail: Each facet admits light in a particular direction. The dark patch represents a pseudopupil in this fixed view.

parts.name: Abdominal back plates
parts.short: These overlapping plates cover the back under the wings.
parts.detail: A series of thin arches forms the dorsal abdominal wall. The plate series lifts away together.

parts.name: Abdominal belly plates
parts.short: Look under the abdomen for the belly plates.
parts.detail: The ventral plates enclose the softer organs. Their pale overlapping edges mark the segment boundaries.

parts.name: Left front leg base
parts.short: Follow this long link from the chest to the grasping leg.
parts.detail: Its inner face bears the European mantis’s dark marking. This individual is represented with a pale center.

parts.name: Left front leg connector
parts.short: This short link connects the long leg base and thigh.
parts.detail: The trochanter sits between coxa and femur. Use it to trace the joint chain even when the leg is folded.

parts.name: Left grasping thigh
parts.short: One side of the spiny trap is a thick thigh.
parts.detail: The thick femur carries muscles and rows of spines. Notice how the tibia closes against the underside.

parts.name: Left grasping shin
parts.short: Drag this folded shin upward to open the front leg.
parts.detail: The shin pivots at the end of the femur. Its recurved tip and opposing spines narrow the space between the two segments as it closes.

parts.name: Left thigh spines
parts.short: These pointed teeth line the grasping thigh.
parts.detail: The spine rows are selectable as a set. Their spacing and count illustrate how the two grasping surfaces fit together.

parts.name: Left shin spines
parts.short: These small points turn toward the thigh when the leg folds.
parts.detail: The marginal spines and larger terminal spur travel with the tibia. The tips are enlarged for exploration.

parts.name: Left front foot
parts.short: The delicate foot extends beyond the spiny shin.
parts.detail: Tarsomeres form the foot beyond the tibia, with a pair of fine terminal claws. It follows the shin as you open the leg.

parts.name: Left shin-closing muscle
parts.short: This bundle pulls the grasping shin closed.
parts.detail: It occupies the thick forefemur. The white terminal thread represents its attachment tendon; the fibers are schematic.

parts.name: Left middle walking leg
parts.short: These long legs support the mantis while its front legs are free.
parts.detail: Trace the bend between femur and tibia. Each walking leg has its own detachable foot.

parts.name: Left middle walking foot
parts.short: The foot ends in tiny gripping claws.
parts.detail: A chain of tarsal segments and the claws at the tip make contact with the ground.

parts.name: Left hind walking leg
parts.short: These long legs support the mantis while its front legs are free.
parts.detail: Trace the bend between femur and tibia. Each walking leg has its own detachable foot.

parts.name: Left hind walking foot
parts.short: The foot ends in tiny gripping claws.
parts.detail: A chain of tarsal segments and the claws at the tip make contact with the ground.

parts.name: Left leathery forewing
parts.short: This narrow green wing lies over the folded flight wing.
parts.detail: Longitudinal veins support the green blade. Its smaller crossveins and pale stigma are schematic.

parts.name: Left folded hindwing
parts.short: A thin fan of wing folds under the green cover.
parts.detail: The pleated membrane can spread during flight. This dissection shows the resting folds.

parts.name: Left tail feeler
parts.short: Feelers at the rear sense movement nearby.
parts.detail: The paired cerci project from the abdominal tip and bear sensory hairs.

parts.name: Brain
parts.short: The brain sits between the two large eyes.
parts.detail: The paired optic lobes flank the central brain. Position and tissue colors here are an educational reconstruction.

parts.name: Belly nerve cord
parts.short: Follow the nerve cord along the underside of the body.
parts.detail: Ganglia along the cord coordinate local movements. The swellings mark a simplified series of nerve centers.

parts.name: Food tube
parts.short: Food travels down this narrow tube from the mouth.
parts.detail: The oesophagus passes through the long prothorax on its way to the crop.

parts.name: Food store
parts.short: A stretchy pouch holds a meal.
parts.detail: The crop can expand after feeding. This model uses a moderately filled pouch informed by dissections of a related mantis.

parts.name: Crop outlet
parts.short: This little chamber leads from the crop into the midgut.
parts.detail: A muscular region regulates passage into the digestive midgut.

parts.name: Digestive tube
parts.short: The mantis digests and absorbs its meal here.
parts.detail: The midgut lies after the foregut valve and before the narrower hindgut.

parts.name: Digestive pouches
parts.short: Small pouches reach along the sides of the gut.
parts.detail: These blind-ended tubes connect near the anterior midgut. The illustrated arrangement follows a related mantis.

parts.name: Rear gut
parts.short: The last part of the gut leads to the rear opening.
parts.detail: The curved hindgut connects the midgut to the rectum. Its bends are simplified.

parts.name: Waste tubes
parts.short: Fine threads help remove waste from the body fluid.
parts.detail: The blind tubules join the gut near the midgut–hindgut boundary. Only a representative bundle is shown.

parts.name: Heart tube
parts.short: A long tube under the back moves body fluid forward.
parts.detail: The abdominal heart continues into an anterior aorta. Breathing tubes deliver oxygen separately.

parts.name: Egg duct
parts.short: These two paths meet and carry eggs toward the rear.
parts.detail: The lateral ducts converge into a common outlet. The reproductive tract is a comparative reconstruction.

parts.name: Left breathing tubes
parts.short: Air reaches the tissues through branching tubes.
parts.detail: The lateral trunks connect a network of airways. Branch thickness is exaggerated so the paths can be followed.

parts.name: Left egg tubes
parts.short: Eggs develop in tubes on each side of the abdomen.
parts.detail: Each ovary is shown as a bundle of ovarioles at an illustrative stage of egg development.

actions.name: Scan
actions.note: Watch the triangular head turn while the walking legs stay planted.

actions.name: Take aim
actions.note: The mantis faces forward and raises its folded grasping legs.

actions.name: Reach and grasp
actions.note: The forelegs sweep out. The spined shins close against the thighs before the legs draw back.
